_doc: Jev question for bin/outbound-precheck.mjs — the relevance gate on every edva-send-curl message. Ported from that file's Sonnet prompt. Jev acts alone on send/suppress; 'modify' always takes Sonnet's text. See docs/jev.md. Kernel definition; an installation's own data/jev-questions/outbound-precheck.json replaces it (lib/jev.mjs jevSiteDef).
notes: Asymmetric risk: a wrong 'send' pings the user with something redundant or contradicted (the failure this gate exists for); a wrong 'suppress' silently drops a real signal or question. Both are costly, so the bar is high and, during the shadow window, a Sonnet 'suppress' overrides a Jev 'send'. Protected intents (p1-email, hum:exercise:*, hum:health:*) and private intents never reach Jev.

verdict.instructions: A programmatic job is about to push proposed_message to the user's phone. Decide whether it goes through. Default to send. Suppress only when: (a) the transcript shows it is wrong, redundant or rude — it asks the user to do something they just said they're doing, nags about something they explained, or contradicts what they just told the agent; (b) long_term_memory directly contradicts it, or shows a job/person already owns that action (a documented delegation). long_term_memory is retrieved by keyword and may return standing policy pages about how the assistant should behave — policy is never itself evidence that THIS message is a repeat; only hum_pings_today, acknowledged_topics_48h, {{owner_id}}_said or the transcript can establish that; (c) acknowledged_topics_48h already covers this SAME subject; (d) hum_pings_today already contains a ping on the SAME subject (same plan, same fact, same question) — sharing a person, pet, place or lane is NOT the same subject. A repeat is not only a same-day event: when {{owner_id}}_said or the transcript carries a DATED earlier message that already made THIS SAME POINT about the SAME named subject, that is a duplicate however many days ago it went out, including when two earlier tellings are merged into one new-looking message; (e) {{owner_id}}_said already answers or settles what it raises. A DEFERRAL ('snooze', 'remind me later', 'not today') is not a settlement: a message about it on a LATER DAY is the reminder the user asked for; a plain refusal still settles the subject; (f) the message promotes a dated outing the user would have to GO to that overlaps a window calendar_now or the transcript shows is already committed to a different plan (judge the overlap, not the day; an all-day entry blocks nothing). A message ABOUT the committed plan itself always sends. A QUESTION to the user on a genuinely new angle sends even if the topic is familiar. authoritative_facts lines marked 'SAME METRO: YES' are correct — never suppress for a location mismatch they say is YES. Judge the part of the message that is NEW, not the recap it opens with. A message whose only new part is the assistant's own internal state (a digest pointer reporting only delivery mechanics, or a run report on its own plumbing) and that asks the user for nothing and carries no hook from inside the email suppresses — unless the user asked for this very change or raised this very problem, or the change is one the user will see. Any ask, however small, sends. Protected intents are never suppressed except on an explicit user revocation.

criteria.send: consistent with all context, or all context is silent on it — the default. A pointer that carries a hook or an ask sends. A report on a problem the user raised or a change they asked for sends.
criteria.suppress: redundant, already settled, already delegated, a same-subject duplicate (today, or the same point about the same named subject on an earlier day), contradicted by the transcript or memory, an outing into an already-committed window, or a report on the assistant's own internal state that offers no hook and asks nothing
criteria.modify: mostly right but needs a small acknowledgment of context that full suppression would lose
